summary.headline: The Select Board declined to retain $100,000 in unissued debt for Breakneck Hill restoration and reviewed Town Meeting preparations.
summary.summary: The Select Board received an update on the town government structure study from consultant Bill Keegan, with a final report anticipated in December following a public forum. The board also reviewed the October 17 Special Town Meeting warrant and unanimously refused a request from the Stewardship Committee and Conservation Commission to retain $100,000 in unissued borrowing authority for Breakneck Hill remediation work. Additionally, the board announced over $1.3 million in state and federal grants, indefinitely postponed a proposed municipal procurement policy, and assigned members to present warrant articles.

topics.title: Town government structure study update
topics.summary: Bill Keegan of Capital Strategic Solutions briefed the board on the town government structure review. He noted Southborough's governance format is common across Massachusetts but discussed options for clearer town administrator authority, potential charter or bylaw updates, and committee realignment. A public listening session is planned for early November, followed by individual board interviews and a final report in December.
key_details: Final report targeted for completion in December.
Initial survey of department heads and committee chairs received high participation.
A public listening session will be held in early November with an online feedback option.
Board members agreed to schedule individual interviews with the consultant.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; public listening session scheduled for early November.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board handled routine community announcements, department updates, and consent agenda items. Announcements included election and early voting dates, community events, and a progress update on Heritage Park equipment.
key_details: Rotary Oktoberfest rescheduled to October 18, 1:15 PM to 5:15 PM, with police details.
Amy Berry was sworn in as interim town clerk on October 1; 1,793 mail-in ballots were mailed.
Heritage Park game box is in place with access code 1727.
Approved consent agenda items B through L, N, and meeting minutes from September 15 and 24.
Approved a $161,545 contract for overhead door replacement, returning over $120,000 from the original $287,500 authorization.
topics.outcome: Consent agenda, minutes, and overhead door contract approved.

topics.title: Neary Elementary School building project options
topics.summary: The board received an update on the Neary Elementary School Building Committee's work. The committee is analyzing five preliminary options ranging from basic systems upgrades to major gymnasium expansions, and plans to present an informational update at Town Meeting.
key_details: Base systems upgrade option is estimated at roughly $33 million.
Most expensive option with gymnasium expansion is estimated at roughly $49 million.
The committee requested an additional analysis for a lower-cost $15 million option.
A brief informational presentation is scheduled for Town Meeting on October 17.
topics.outcome: Update accepted; joint meeting with School Committee and Advisory Committee to be scheduled.

topics.title: State and federal grant awards and Costco alcohol license
topics.summary: The town administrator announced more than $1.3 million in outside grant awards, highlighted by a $1.1 million MassWorks grant for Southville Road. The governor also signed special legislation authorizing an additional alcohol license for Costco, and other awards funded fire safety gear and regional corridor planning.
key_details: Received a $1.1 million MassWorks grant to replace 1,300 feet of water main on Southville Road with 12-inch ductile iron pipe.
Special act signed by the governor granting an alcohol license for Costco, with authority to issue it until October 4, 2028.
Awarded $150,000 jointly with Westborough for a Route 9 and I-495 business corridor study.
Received an $86,857.14 FEMA grant for Fire Department hose replacement.
Received $20,559 in highway traffic safety funds for police enforcement overtime and LiDAR equipment.
topics.outcome: Grants and legislative approval announced; no board vote required.
topics.why_it_matters: The town secured over $1.3 million in outside state and federal funding to upgrade critical water mains, fire equipment, and traffic safety without local tax impact.

topics.title: Special Town Meeting warrant review and Breakneck Hill debt rescission
topics.summary: The board reviewed warrant articles for the October 17 Special Town Meeting and considered a request from the Conservation Commission and Stewardship Committee to modify Article 6. The committees requested holding back $100,000 in unissued borrowing authority for additional Breakneck Hill dump cleanup and habitat restoration. The board unanimously opposed offering or supporting any floor amendment to reduce the rescission, noting $176,000 in borrowed funds remains available.
key_details: Article 6 seeks to rescind $727,960 in authorized but unborrowed debt from the Breakneck Hill remediation project.
The town previously borrowed $3.6 million of a $4.327 million total authorization, leaving roughly $176,000 unspent in cash.
The Stewardship Committee sought to keep $100,000 authorized (rescinding $627,960) to fund additional meadow restoration and road repairs.
Board members agreed that the original environmental remediation is complete and declined to sponsor a floor amendment.
Board members were assigned to make the motions on Town Meeting floor for Articles 1, 2, 6, and 7.
topics.outcome: The board unanimously declined to support amending Article 6 on town meeting floor.
topics.why_it_matters: Full rescission of $727,960 in authorized borrowing closes out long-standing remediation debt capacity and prevents additional town borrowing for property landscaping.

topics.title: Proposed procurement and conflict of interest policy
topics.summary: The board discussed a draft procurement and conflict of interest policy intended to standardize town purchasing practices. Members criticized the draft as overly rigid and redundant with existing state ethics statutes, pointing out unreasonable mandates such as requiring audited financial statements from small contractors.
key_details: Draft policy included strict pre-qualification requirements and audited financial statements for contractors.
Members noted that statutory conflict of interest rules and mandatory ethics training already govern town operations.
Revisions from town counsel removed confidentiality language but simply duplicated state law text.
topics.outcome: The board agreed by consensus to table the policy indefinitely.
